sentences.text: This creature grew to a maximum size of roughly sixty centimeters in length.
It featured a tail fin with an uneven shape and prominent spines on its upper fins.
The front fins possessed just two foundational bones, missing a specific structure common in other cartilaginous fish.
Remains of the single known species, Tristychius arcuatus, were found in Scotland.
The name Tristychius was first given by Agassiz in the year 1837.
Researchers believe it was a bottom-dwelling hunter that used suction to capture food.
It is a member of the class Chondrichthyes.
Scientists place it in the family Tristychiidae, grouping it with the genus Acronemus.
While once thought to be a hybodont, a 2016 study moved it to the basal euselachian group.
This animal lived between 346.7 and 326.9 million years ago.
